title: Proper Cohomological Descent And Constructible Hypercovers

items.title: Bicosimplicial total complexes agree with diagonal totalization
items.statement: For a bicosimplicial complex $K^{p,r,q}$ of modules over a commutative ring, with $p,r\geq0$ and one fixed lower bound $q\geq a$, the alternating-face total complex and the diagonal alternating-face total complex are naturally chain-homotopy equivalent: $$\operatorname{Tot}_{p,r,q}K^{p,r,q}\simeq\operatorname{Tot}_{n,q}K^{n,n,q}.$$ On the left total degree is $p+r+q$ and differential is $\delta_h+(-1)^p\delta_v+(-1)^{p+r}d$; on the right total degree is $n+q$ and differential is $\delta_{\mathrm{diag}}+(-1)^nd$. These comparisons preserve augmentation and apply to coherent derived diagrams after a supplied functorial strict resolution. They require no dimensional finiteness of the coefficient modules and no choice principle. Normalization can be applied on either side without changing the conclusion.
items.strategy: Sources: Dugger-Hollander-Isaksen, Hypercovers and simplicial presheaves, Appendix A (acyclic-model comparison of bisimplicial totals, PDF pp. 35-36, read in full) and Stacks Project, Simplicial Methods, Sections 23 and 27 (normalization, simplex and prism identities, read in full). Write [[def-chain-complex-in-an-abelian-category]] for complexes and chain homotopies and [[def-direct-sum-total-complex-of-a-double-complex]] for Tot. Step 1 (specified contractions on universal models). The evaluation $M\mapsto M_{p,r}$ is represented by the free bisimplicial module $Q_{p,r}$ on $\Delta[p]\times\Delta[r]$: an element $x\in M_{p,r}$ defines the unique homomorphism sending the universal generator to $x$. The diagonal alternating-face complex of $Q_{p,r}$ is the simplicial chain complex of the product of the two standard simplices, while the double total complex is the tensor product of their separate simplicial chain complexes. Both have a specified contraction onto the vertex $(0,0)$: the monotone contraction to the initial vertex gives a simplicial homotopy whose chain homotopy is the prism of [[lem-simplicial-normalization-prism-and-trivial-fibration-criterion]], and the unnormalized point complex is contracted by $e_j\mapsto e_{j+1}$ for odd $j$ and zero for even $j$; for the tensor product the contraction is $H(x\otimes y)=h(x)\otimes y+(-1)^{|x|}e(x)\otimes h(y)$, where $e$ is the vertex projector, and direct expansion gives $\partial H+H\partial=1-e\otimes e$. Every positive-degree cycle and augmentation-zero degree-zero cycle in either model thus has a specified finite filling. Step 2 (natural maps by universal recursion). Construct a natural chain map from the diagonal complex to the double total complex recursively. In degree zero it is the identity on $M_{0,0}$. On the universal diagonal degree-$n$ generator of $Q_{n,n}$, the already constructed image of its boundary is a cycle, of augmentation zero if $n=1$; fill this cycle by the contraction of Step 1, and send an arbitrary element of $M_{n,n}$ to the image of this filling under its unique representing map. This is additive and natural because the representing map is linear in that element, and its boundary is the required lower-degree image. The same recursion on a universal total degree-$n$ generator in each $Q_{p,r}$ with $p+r=n$ constructs a chain map in the reverse direction. Both maps are the identity in degree zero. Step 3 (homotopy inverse). Any two natural maps constructed this way that agree in degree zero are naturally chain homotopic: on a universal degree-$n$ generator $z$, the difference of the two maps on $z$ minus the already chosen homotopy on its boundary is an augmentation-zero cycle, filled by the same specified model contraction, and evaluated on arbitrary elements using their representing maps; this gives $\partial H+H\partial=f-g$ in every degree. Apply this to the two composite maps and the identities. All maps and homotopies are finite linear combinations of face and degeneracy operators, so no unspecified filling is selected. Step 4 (opposite category, no duality). Reverse those finite operator formulas to obtain the cochain maps and cochain homotopies for bicosimplicial modules: a universal operator identity is an equality in the free additive category on $\Delta\times\Delta$, and reversing every arrow turns a simplicial identity into its cosimplicial identity and reverses the direction of each natural map. Hence the two composite identities and their homotopies remain valid for every bicosimplicial module without taking an algebraic dual or imposing finite-dimensionality. Apply them separately in each internal degree $q$; they commute with the internal differential by naturality, and the signs in the Statement make the internal terms cancel in the homotopy equation, since each cochain homotopy lowers $p+r$ by one. Step 5 (finiteness, totals and normalization). In total degree $m$, only $p+r\leq m-a$ contributes on the left and $n\leq m-a$ on the right, so every map and homotopy uses finitely many coefficient terms and [[prop-sum-and-product-totalisations-agree-on-finite-diagonal-double-complexes]] permits either sum or product total notation. Normalization is a natural homotopy equivalence by [[lem-simplicial-normalization-prism-and-trivial-fibration-criterion]], also in the opposite cosimplicial category, so it may be applied on either side. The constructions preserve the unique degree-zero augmentation and commute with morphisms of complexes; a supplied strict derived resolution is used only to present a coherent diagram, and the natural homotopy equivalence descends to the derived category independently of that presentation.

items.title: Proper surjections have cohomological descent for constructible field sheaves
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the supplied injective-resolution six-functor construction. Let $f:Y\to X$ be a proper surjective morphism of finite-type complex algebraic varieties, and let $F\in D^b_c(X;k)$ for a field $k$. Write $Y_p=Y\times_X\cdots\times_XY$ with $p+1$ factors, $f_p:Y_p\to X$, and $F_p=f_p^*F$. In the analytic topology of [[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]] the natural augmented derived Cech map is a quasi-isomorphism: $$F\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Tot}_{p\geq0}Rf_{p*}F_p.$$ Here totalization is the normalized or unnormalized alternating-face total supplied by the simplicial-derived construction. There is one fixed lower cochain bound; consequently its diagonals are finite in every degree. The claim commutes with arbitrary algebraic base change and coefficient morphisms. In particular $R\Gamma(X,F)\simeq\operatorname{Tot}_pR\Gamma(Y_p,F_p)$. Individual fibers of $f$ need not be cohomologically acyclic, connected, or smooth.
items.strategy: Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Sources: Dugger-Hollander-Isaksen Appendix A (proper Cech descent by stalk contraction; PDF pp. 35-36, read in full) and Stacks Project, Hypercoverings, Lemma 3.9 and Lemmas 4.2-4.5 (general-site cohomological descent; PDF pp. 5-10, read in full). [F1] The coherent six-operation contract over an arbitrary coefficient field for analytic algebraic maps on bounded constructible complexes is [[thm-analytic-sheaf-six-operations-have-coherent-base-change-projection-and-trace]]: it gives exact inverse image, ordinary proper base change, its naturality for all Cech faces and degeneracies, and the identification of $f_p^*F$ restricted to a geometric fiber with the constant pullback of $F_x$. The coefficient category is [[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]], and the restriction of the operations to it over every field, with each pulled coefficient again bounded below, is [[lem-analytic-constructible-sheaves-admit-coherent-six-operations]]. [F2] [[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]] supplies the functorial simplicial-derived total model with a uniform internal lower bound and finite-degree truncations; its local-section descent conclusion is not used as proper descent. [F3] [[thm-bounded-filtered-complex-spectral-sequence-abuts-to-filtered-homology]] gives convergence for degreewise finite filtrations, with cohomological reindexing. [A1] AC is inherited only by the supplied resolution construction; selecting one point for the stalk argument requires only a single nonempty-set selection, not a simultaneously chosen family of sections. Step 1.1 (bounded model and finite diagonals). Choose a lower bound $a$ for the cochain model of $F$; exact pullback preserves it and right-derived pushforward gives a functorial double model in degrees $p\geq0$, $q\geq a$, so in total degree $m$ there are only $0\leq p\leq m-a$ terms. Take the cone of the augmented map and filter by $p$, still bounded below after placing the augmentation in column $p=-1$. Stalks commute with its finite pieces, so by the finite-filtration spectral sequence of [F3] it suffices to prove exactness of every augmented horizontal stalk row after taking internal cohomology. Step 2.1 (stalk rows and one chosen point). Fix $x\in X$ and put $K=F_x$; surjectivity gives a nonempty proper fiber $S=Y_x$, and proper base change identifies the augmented horizontal row in internal degree $q$ with $H^q(K)\to H^q(S,K)\to H^q(S^2,K)\to\cdots$, where $K$ on each $S^{p+1}$ is its constant derived pullback from the point; [F1] intertwines all deletion and repetition maps. Pick one point $y\in S$; for $p\geq1$ let $j_p:S^p\to S^{p+1}$ insert $y$ as first coordinate and let $j_0:\mathrm{pt}\to S$ be this point. Pullback gives maps $h_p=j_p^*:H^q(S^{p+1},K)\to H^q(S^p,K)$, with $h_0$ landing in $H^q(K)$. No assertion that any positive cohomology group of $S$ vanishes is made. Step 3.1 (explicit contraction). If $d_i:S^{p+2}\to S^{p+1}$ deletes coordinate $i$, the insertion identities are $d_0j_{p+1}=\operatorname{id}$ and $d_ij_{p+1}=j_pd_{i-1}$ for $i>0$. On the augmented row put $\delta_p=\sum_{i=0}^{p+1}(-1)^id_i^*$ and let $\delta_{-1}:H^q(K)\to H^q(S,K)$ be constant pullback. The displayed identities give $h_{p+1}\delta_p+\delta_{p-1}h_p=\operatorname{id}$ for every $p\geq0$, and $h_0\delta_{-1}=\operatorname{id}$: the $i=0$ term is the identity and the terms $i>0$ are precisely the negatives of $\delta_{p-1}h_p$. Every horizontal stalk row is thus contracted, including its augmentation and every internal degree $q$; this uses functorial pullback on cohomology, not an acyclicity assumption about individual fibers or a global section of $f$. Step 4.1 (conclusion). The horizontal spectral sequence of the augmented cone has zero next page at every stalk by Step 3.1; its filtration is finite in each total degree by Step 1.1, so [F3] gives zero stalk cohomology of the cone. A complex of sheaves with all cohomology stalks zero is acyclic, proving the asserted quasi-isomorphism. All algebraic base changes of $f$ remain proper surjective and the same base-change identifications prove the pulled-back assertion without choosing compatible points; naturality of the augmentation follows from its units and face maps. Applying derived global sections to the supplied finite-diagonal total model gives the global statement. AC is inherited exactly through [A1].

items.title: Proper hypercovers compute constructible derived cohomology
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the supplied six-functor resolutions. Let $X_\bullet\to X$ be an augmented simplicial finite-type complex algebraic variety ([[def-simplicial-object-and-simplicial-commutative-ring]], [[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]]). Assume $X_0\to X$ is proper surjective and, for each $p>0$, $X_p\to(\operatorname{cosk}_{p-1}\operatorname{sk}_{p-1}X_\bullet)_p$ is proper surjective over $X$, where skeleton and coskeleton are the standard finite-limit constructions of the simplicial category and the target is the matching object. Such an object is a proper hypercover; no smoothness or fiber acyclicity is assumed. For $F\in D^b_c(X;k)$ over a field, and $a_p:X_p\to X$, the augmentation gives $$F\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Tot}_{p\geq0}Ra_{p*}a_p^*F,\qquad R\Gamma(X,F)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Tot}_{p\geq0}R\Gamma(X_p,a_p^*F).$$ There is a natural strongly convergent spectral sequence $E_1^{p,q}=H^q(X_p,a_p^*F)\Rightarrow H^{p+q}(X,F)$. If $F$ has cochain lower bound $a$, every diagonal $p+q=m$ is finite; degree $m$ and its differential are determined by levels through $p=m-a+1$. All proper-hypercover refinements induce the same comparison via the base object; any two such hypercovers have a proper common refinement. For $F=k_X$, $a=0$, this is the first-quadrant spectral sequence required for smooth-projective hyperresolutions.
items.strategy: Assume AC as inherited from the supplied six-functor resolutions ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Sources: Dugger-Hollander-Isaksen Appendix A Proposition A.4, Lemma A.5 and Corollaries A.7-A.9 (bounded-hypercover bisimplicial Cech and retract argument; PDF pp. 35-38, read in full) and Stacks Project, Hypercoverings, Lemmas 4.2-4.5 and 5.1-5.3 (PDF pp. 5-10, read in full). [F1] [[lem-proper-surjective-maps-have-cohomological-descent-for-constructible-field-sheaves]] proves actual proper Cech descent, including arbitrary base change for bounded constructible coefficient complexes over any field. [F2] [[lem-bicosimplicial-derived-total-complex-agrees-with-diagonal-totalization]] supplies the natural alternating-face diagonal/double-total homotopy equivalence. [F3] [[thm-analytic-sheaf-six-operations-have-coherent-base-change-projection-and-trace]] and [[lem-analytic-constructible-sheaves-admit-coherent-six-operations]] supply the ordinary coherent operations on bounded algebraically constructible complexes ([[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]]), while [[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]] supplies functorial coherent derived diagrams, strict simplicial resolutions, right-derived composition and their uniformly bounded-below total model; [[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]] fixes the analytic topology of the varieties. [F4] [[thm-bounded-filtered-complex-spectral-sequence-abuts-to-filtered-homology]] gives convergence for degreewise finite filtrations. [A1] AC is inherited only through the resolution inputs and [F1]; the finite coskeleton, product and retract constructions below make no new arbitrary selections. The proof reconstructs the matching-map vocabulary of [[def-simplicial-object-and-simplicial-commutative-ring]] inline: for the augmented simplicial variety $X_\bullet\to X$, $\operatorname{sk}_{p-1}$ is the simplicial truncation and $\operatorname{cosk}_{p-1}$ its right adjoint, formed by the finite limit formulas, and the matching object at level $p$ is $M_p=\lim_{[p]\to[k],k<p}X_k$. Step 1.1 (height zero). Let $U\to X$ be a bounded proper hypercover of height zero, that is $U=\operatorname{cosk}_0U_0$; this is the Cech nerve of the proper surjection $U_0\to X$, so [F1] proves both the sheaf and global augmentations. Suppose inductively they are proved for all bounded heights at most $n$, and let $U=\operatorname{cosk}_{n+1}U$ have height $n+1$. Put $V=\operatorname{cosk}_nU$: it is a proper hypercover of height at most $n$, since its original matching maps through degree $n$ are unchanged and its later matching maps are isomorphisms, so the inductive hypothesis applies to $V$. Step 2.1 (levelwise proper surjectivity). For every $j$, $U_j\to V_j$ is proper surjective. For $j\leq n$ it is the identity; in higher degree it is the map $\operatorname{Hom}(\operatorname{sk}_{n+1}\Delta[j],U)\to\operatorname{Hom}(\operatorname{sk}_n\Delta[j],U)$ between finite matching limits, and attaching the finitely many nondegenerate $(n+1)$-faces of $\Delta[j]$ to its $n$-skeleton makes it a Cartesian pullback of the finite product of the matching map $U_{n+1}\to M_{n+1}U$. A finite product over $X$ of proper surjections and any base change thereof is proper surjective; no local sections are required. Step 3.1 (bisimplicial Cech model). Form $W_{r,j}=U_j\times_{V_j}\cdots\times_{V_j}U_j$ with $r+1$ factors, horizontally the Cech nerve of $U_j\to V_j$, and pull coefficients from $X$ throughout. By [F1] and Step 2.1 every horizontally augmented derived row computes the coefficient complex on $V_j$, before and after pushing to $X$, so the induced augmentation into the double total is a quasi-isomorphism: apply [F4] to the triple-complex model of [F3], whose degrees $r,j\geq0$, $q\geq a$ have finite total diagonals. The inductive augmentation for $V$ then gives $F\simeq\operatorname{Tot}_{r,j}Ra_{W_{r,j}*}F_{W_{r,j}}$ and the analogous global statement; by [F2] this double total is naturally equivalent to the total on the diagonal $D_j=W_{j,j}$. Step 4.1 (retract over $X$). The bounded hypercover $U$ is a retract over $X$ of $D$: the map $i:U\to D$ repeats the same $U_j$ point in all $j+1$ horizontal factors, and through degree $n$ the map $U_j\to V_j$ is the identity, so $D_j=U_j$ there; in degree $n+1$ choose the first projection $D_{n+1}\to U_{n+1}$, whose faces and degeneracies agree with the degree-$\leq n$ identity maps because every horizontal factor has the same image in $V$ and those lower-degree maps are identities. This defines a map of $(n+1)$-truncations, and the universal property $U=\operatorname{cosk}_{n+1}U$ extends it uniquely to $r:D\to U$; the composite $ri$ is the identity through degree $n+1$, hence in every degree by the same universal property. Coefficient pullback reverses these maps, so the augmented total for $U$ is a retract of the augmented total for $D$, and a retract of an acyclic cone is acyclic. This completes the bounded-height induction. Step 5.1 (arbitrary height by truncation). For an arbitrary proper hypercover $U$, its $N$-coskeleton $U^{(N)}=\operatorname{cosk}_N\operatorname{sk}_NU$ is a bounded proper hypercover, so Step 4.1 applies to it; the map $U\to U^{(N)}$ is the identity through simplicial degree $N$. In the strict derived total model every internal degree is at least $a$, so total degrees $m-1,m,m+1$ use only simplicial degrees at most $m-a+1$. Choosing $N\geq\max(0,m-a+1)$ makes the totals for $U$ and $U^{(N)}$ have the same objects and differentials in these three degrees, hence the same degree-$m$ cohomology and the same augmentation maps; since this holds for every $m$, the augmentation for $U$ is a quasi-isomorphism. This is a finite-degree truncation argument, not an interchange of stalks or cohomology with an unjustified infinite product. Step 6.1 (spectral sequence and convergence). Filter the global total by simplicial degree. Its first page is $E_1^{p,q}=H^q(X_p,a_p^*F)$ with alternating pullback by faces as first differential. In degree $m$ its filtration has only $0\leq p\leq m-a$ nonzero pieces, so [F4] identifies the stationary page with the finite associated graded of $H^m(X,F)$, proving strong convergence; no finite-dimensionality of the individual $H^q$ groups is needed. Step 7.1 (refinements and constant coefficients). For two proper hypercovers $U,V$ over $X$, their levelwise product $R_j=U_j\times_XV_j$ is a common proper hypercover: finite matching limits commute with products, so each matching map of $R$ is the product over $X$ of the matching maps of $U$ and $V$ and is proper surjective, and its projections give the two refinements. By Step 5.1 both augmentations identify their totals with the same coefficient complex on $X$, so the comparison maps coincide after those identifications. A smooth-projective refinement is a separate supplied construction: the product of smooth maps over singular $X$ need not be smooth. For $F=k_X$ the lower bound is $a=0$ and the page is exactly the stated first-quadrant spectral sequence. AC is inherited precisely through [A1].

title: Proper Cohomological Descent And Constructible Hypercovers Examples

items.title: Proper Cech descent does not require acyclic fibers
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice; it is inherited from the descent lemma and from the field-dual corollary. Let $k$ be a field and let $S=\mathbb P^1(\mathbb C)$ be the complex projective line, realized as the classical complex algebraic variety obtained by gluing two affine lines along their punctured overlaps by $z=1/w$, with its analytic topology (equivalently, the Riemann sphere $\widehat{\mathbb C}=\mathbb C\cup\{\infty\}$). Then the unique morphism $f:S\to\mathrm{pt}$ is proper surjective, the single fiber $S$ satisfies $H^2(S;k)\cong k\neq0$ and is therefore not cohomologically acyclic, and yet the augmented Cech complex computes the constant sheaf: the unaugmented product total $\operatorname{Tot}_{p\geq0}R\Gamma(S^{p+1},k)$ has cohomology $k$ in degree $0$ and zero in all other degrees. In every internal degree $q$ the augmented row $H^q(k)\to H^q(S,k)\to H^q(S^2,k)\to\cdots$ is contracted by inserting one chosen point as first coordinate, even though the $q=2$ row contains the nonzero group $H^2(S;k)$ at $p=0$.
items.strategy: Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Step 1 (the space). Construct $S=\mathbb P^1(\mathbb C)$ as the classical complex algebraic variety obtained by gluing the two affine models $\mathbb C$ with coordinate $z$ and $\mathbb C$ with coordinate $w$ along the principal open subsets $z\neq0$ and $w\neq0$ by the regular isomorphism $z=1/w$: the gluing of two affine models along an open subset is a classical prevariety by the definition, it is separated (the diagonal is closed, checked on the two charts), and the finite two-chart cover makes it finite type over $\mathbb C$ ([[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]]); it carries the analytic topology of [[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]]. The same two charts identify $S$ with the Riemann sphere $\widehat{\mathbb C}=\mathbb C\cup\{\infty\}$ of [[def-one-point-compactification]]: the $z$-chart is a homeomorphism onto $\mathbb C$, the $w$-chart identifies the remaining point with $\infty$, and the transition $w=1/z$ is the corresponding homeomorphism of the pointed charts. Hence the analytic topology of $S$ is the one-point compactification topology and $S$ is compact Hausdorff ([[thm-one-point-compactification-properties]]). Step 2 (the map is proper surjective). $f$ is surjective because $S$ is nonempty. It is a projective morphism of classical varieties: the identity is a closed immersion $S\hookrightarrow \mathrm{pt}\times\mathbb P^1(\mathbb C)$ and the projection to the point is the structure map ([[def-projective-morphism-classical]]); projective algebraic morphisms are proper in the analytic topology, and the descent lemma uses that properness ([[thm-complex-algebraic-varieties-and-maps-admit-compatible-finite-stratifications]], [[lem-proper-surjective-maps-have-cohomological-descent-for-constructible-field-sheaves]]). Step 3 (the fiber is not acyclic). Stereographic projection is a homeomorphism $\widehat{\mathbb C}\to S^2$ ([[thm-stereographic-projection-riemann-sphere-homeomorphism]]); a homeomorphism is a homotopy equivalence, so it induces isomorphisms on singular homology ([[thm-homotopy-equivalences-induce-isomorphisms-on-singular-homology]]). Thus $H_2(S;k)\cong H_2(S^2;k)\cong k$ by [[cor-homology-of-spheres]], and the field-dual corollary gives $H^2(S;k)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_k(H_2(S;k),k)\cong k$ ([[cor-cohomology-over-a-field-is-dual-to-homology-over-that-field]]); in particular the single fiber of $f$ is not cohomologically acyclic. Step 4 (the rows are still contracted). The fiber of $f$ over the unique point is $S$ and the fiber powers are $S^{p+1}$. Choose one point $y\in S$ and let $j_p:S^p\to S^{p+1}$ insert $y$ as first coordinate for $p\geq1$, with $j_0:\mathrm{pt}\to S$ this point; putting $h_p=j_p^*$ and letting $\delta$ be the alternating sum of deletion pullbacks, the insertion identities $d_0j_{p+1}=\operatorname{id}$ and $d_ij_{p+1}=j_pd_{i-1}$ for $i>0$ give $h_{p+1}\delta_p+\delta_{p-1}h_p=\operatorname{id}$ in every internal degree $q$, including the augmentation. So the $q=2$ row, whose $p=0$ term is the nonzero group $H^2(S;k)\cong k$, is nevertheless exact with only the augmentation surviving. Step 5 (conclusion). By [[lem-proper-surjective-maps-have-cohomological-descent-for-constructible-field-sheaves]] applied to $f$ and the constant sheaf $k$, the augmented Cech total computes $k$: the unaugmented product total $\operatorname{Tot}_{p\geq0}R\Gamma(S^{p+1},k)$ has cohomology $k$ in degree $0$ and zero elsewhere. The example shows that proper Cech descent does not require acyclic fibers: the nonvanishing $H^2$ of the fiber is retained throughout the contracted rows and does not obstruct the descent quasi-isomorphism.

items.title: Hypercover total degree uses only a finite matching truncation
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the proper-hypercover theorem. Let $X_\bullet\to X$ be a proper hypercover and let $F$ be a coefficient complex in $D^b_c(X;k)$ with cochain lower bound $a$ ([[def-simplicial-object-and-simplicial-commutative-ring]]). Then the cohomology of the total complex in degree $m$, and its differential, are determined by the simplicial levels $p\leq m-a+1$ only; every hypercover truncation $\operatorname{cosk}_N\operatorname{sk}_NX_\bullet$ with $N\geq m-a+1$ computes the same $H^m(X,F)$. In particular for the constant sheaf $F=k_X$, where $a=0$, degree $n$ uses only levels through $n+1$. Level $n$ alone does not suffice: the differential out of the term $(p,q)=(n,0)$ of the Cech complex lands in the level $n+1$ term $(n+1,0)$.
items.strategy: Assume AC as inherited from [[thm-proper-hypercovers-compute-constructible-derived-cohomology]]. Step 1 (degree bookkeeping). In the total complex of the hypercover, the term in bidegree $(p,q)$ has $p\geq0$ and $q\geq a$; it contributes to total degree $p+q$. For a fixed total degree $m$, this gives $0\leq p\leq m-a$. The differentials entering and leaving total degree $m$ involve terms of total degree $m-1$, $m$ and $m+1$, so the largest simplicial level appearing there is $p=m+1-a$. Step 2 (truncation agrees). By [[thm-proper-hypercovers-compute-constructible-derived-cohomology]], the comparison of $X_\bullet$ with its $N$-coskeleton truncation $\operatorname{cosk}_N\operatorname{sk}_NX_\bullet$ is the identity through simplicial degree $N$, and the total complex in a fixed total degree uses only finitely many levels. Choosing $N\geq m-a+1$ makes the two total complexes agree in degrees $m-1$, $m$, $m+1$, hence they have the same $H^m$ and the same augmentation maps there; since $m$ was arbitrary, every truncation above the stated bound computes the same cohomology. Step 3 (constant coefficients and sharpness). For $F=k_X$ the lower bound is $a=0$, so degree $n$ uses levels through $n+1$. The bound is sharp: the term $(p,q)=(n,0)$ is $H^0(X_n,k)$, and its outgoing differential is the alternating sum of face pullbacks into the level $n+1$ term $H^0(X_{n+1},k)$ of total degree $n+1$; knowing $H^n$ requires this differential, so level $n$ alone is not enough. No infinite product and no separate convergence argument is used beyond the quoted total-degree statements of the theorem.
